reference.title: Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Upper Arms, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the dumbbells lower beside the head, exhale as the elbows straighten.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps in the range, then a heavier dumbbell (2-5% steps), then a slower lowering

cues.text: Lie on the bench, feet flat on the floor, a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, arms straight up over the shoulders.
Breathe in and bend only the elbows: the dumbbells travel back and down beside the head.
Dumbbells beside the ears, upper arms still vertical, elbows pointing at the ceiling.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows, moving only the forearms.
Arms straight but not locked, dumbbells over the shoulders; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging (turning it into a pullover)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling; only the forearms move.
Keep the elbows about shoulder width apart.
Lower them beside the head, not over the face; use a lighter weight if control slips.

mistakes.mistake: Lower back arching off the bench
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the feet planted and the ribs down.
Pause briefly beside the head, then press smoothly.

kinematics.norm: Straight but not locked at the top; lower until the dumbbells are beside the head, about 100-120 degrees of elbow flexion (clinical opinion). Activation and relative force were matched across the three heads at 90 degrees of flexion or more (PLoS ONE 2021)
Upper arms vertical (about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion) and still; at 90 degrees and above the medial head carries the most force (Kholinne 2018)
The dumbbells pass beside the head, never over the face (clinical opinion)
Head, upper back and buttocks on the bench, feet flat on the floor (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s lowering and 1-1.5 s pressing (clinical opinion); the EMG comparison used sets of 7 reps at 70% of 1RM (Boehler 2011)

sources.title: GymVisual #035112, Dumbbell Lying Triceps Extension, video (movement reference)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)
Effect of elbow joint angles on electromyographic activity versus force relationships of synergistic muscles of the triceps brachii (PLoS ONE 2021; PMC8174684)

cautions: Elbow pain: use a lighter dumbbell, shorten the range or switch to a cable pushdown (clinical opinion).
Control the dumbbells over the head; never lower them toward the face.
Hand the dumbbells off by bringing them to the chest and sitting up, not by dropping them beside the bench.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Elbow discomfort: angle the upper arms slightly back toward the head, or use a neutral grip (as here).
Lower back arching: put the feet on the end of the bench.

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Does all of the work: lowers the dumbbells under control and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell version the long and lateral heads differed significantly in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical (about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion) the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Does all of the work: lowers the dumbbells under control and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell version the long and lateral heads differed significantly in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical (about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion) the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the upper arms vertical as the dumbbells travel back toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the upper arms vertical as the dumbbells travel back toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the handles and keep the wrists straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the handles and keep the wrists straight.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the lower back from arching off the bench.
